Intro description: Hello! 👋 I’m Alex, a dedicated financial advisor with a passion for helping clients achieve their financial dreams through personalized, tax-optimized strategies. With a background in banking and years of experience in financial planning, I bring a unique blend of expertise and empathy to my work, focusing on income planning and tax efficiency to guide clients toward their goals. My journey to becoming a financial advisor was driven by a desire to make a meaningful impact, building trusted relationships that empower pre-retirees to plan confidently for their future. Outside of work, you can find me hitting the golf course, playing pickup basketball, or getting in a good workout. Family time is especially important to me, and I love nothing more than cheering on my daughter at her soccer games and my son on his football team. On weekends, you can often find me outside by the grill, experimenting with new BBQ techniques and smoking meat for friends and family.
Quote: My approach is all about creating personalized, tax-smart strategies that empower my clients to achieve their dreams with confidence. By taking the time to truly understand their unique goals, both short and long-term, and leveraging advanced planning tools, I guide them through every financial decision, celebrating each milestone we reach together as if it were my own.
Service eyebrow 1: TAKE CONTROL OF YOUR FINANCIAL FUTURE
Service description 1: Personalized wealth management helps our clients protect their assets. We use a holistic approach to financial planning that integrates tax strategy, trust & estate planning, and risk management.
Service eyebrow 2: STRIVING TO MINIMIZE YOUR TAX BURDEN
Service description 2: We aim to take the ambiguity out of tax planning by utilizing tax-reducing strategies that encompass your overall tax liability. We do it by putting together a game plan that is specific to your needs.
Service description 3: Understand your income with an annual plan showing where cash flow is generated, and why. This weaves together Restricted Stock Units (RSU) flows, stock option exercises, long-term capital gains, Roth Conversions, etc.
Full description:
With a foundation of experience in banking and a deep passion for personalized financial guidance, Alex has dedicated his career to helping pre-retirees achieve their dreams through thoughtful, tax-optimized strategies. His expertise in income planning and tax efficiency, paired with advanced financial tools, allows him to craft tailored plans that align with each client’s unique goals. What drives Alex is building meaningful relationships and celebrating the joy of seeing clients gain confidence in their financial future.

Alex claims the most rewarding part of his work is witnessing the relief and excitement clients feel when they achieve a milestone they’ve planned together—whether it’s preparing for a secure retirement, funding a dream purchase, or creating a legacy for their loved ones. Every step of the journey reinforces his commitment to providing clear, strategic support that makes a real difference. His goal is simple, to help clients keep more of what they earn and invest with purpose, so they can live the life they envision.

Outside of work, Alex enjoys staying active, whether that’s hitting the golf course, playing pickup basketball, or getting in a good workout. Family time is especially important, and he loves nothing more than cheering on his daughter at her soccer games and his son on his football team. On weekends, you can often find Alex outside by the grill, experimenting with new BBQ techniques and smoking meat for friends and family.
FAQ answer 1: I began my career in banking, but I quickly realized that I wanted to make a deeper impact by working with individuals and families on a more personal and comprehensive level - that is where my true passion lies. That realization led me to financial planning and ultimately becoming a financial advisor. In this role, I’ve found the perfect balance: building meaningful relationships while helping clients with financial decisions that align with their goals. It’s incredibly rewarding to provide the kind of personalized support that can truly change someone’s financial future.
FAQ answer 2: I primarily work with pre-retirees who are established in their careers and recognize the importance of proactive planning. These clients often come to me with both short- and long-term goals and they understand that having a professional guide can help them optimize their strategy and potentially reach those goals more efficiently. They’re thoughtful about their future and value expert support in making confident, informed decisions.
FAQ answer 3: My areas of expertise are income planning and tax optimization. I believe these are two critical components, and I incorporate them into every client’s financial strategy, whether they’re preparing for retirement or already enjoying it. I leverage advanced financial planning software to analyze income flows and tax implications, helping my clients make informed decisions. My goal is to create tailored strategies that not only support their lifestyle but also maximize tax efficiency over the long term.
FAQ answer 4: My strategies are always tailored to each of my client’s unique situations, but a core part of my approach is helping my clients understand how their income, savings, and distribution decisions impact their overall financial picture. I use tax and income planning tools to illustrate how different strategies can affect both their short- and long-term goals. By modeling various scenarios, I can help clients make informed decisions that align with their values, minimize tax exposure, and support a more efficient path to financial independence.
FAQ answer 5: My favorite part of working with clients is seeing the joy and relief that comes when they achieve a goal we’ve planned for together. Whether it’s saving for a major purchase, preparing for retirement, or creating a legacy for the next generation, I truly take pride in being part of that journey. In my opinion, there’s nothing more rewarding than watching one of my clients feel confident and excited about their future, and knowing I had a hand in helping make that possible. Each milestone we reach together deepens our relationship and reinforces why I love what I do.
FAQ answer 6: What I value most about working with Savvy is the ability it gives me to truly focus on my clients. The platform’s streamlined tools and technology allow me to work more efficiently, I am able to complete important tasks faster so I can spend more time focused on building relationships and offering thoughtful guidance to my clients. The support model at Savvy empowers me to deliver a high level of service while ensuring every strategy I create is both personalized and forward-thinking. It’s a structure that puts my clients first, and that’s what matters most.

Joshua grew up in Reno, Nevada, with a constant curiosity and avid observance of the world around him. This curiosity sparked his understanding of wealth management, always striving to read about and refine his financial models and investment strategies.

Joshua’s financial journey started from the ground up like many of his clients. After learning the ins and outs of the financial world, Joshua eventually co-founded a trust company in 1999 and a financial advisory firm in 2006.

Leaning on the experience he gained during his financial journey, Joshua is passionate about guiding others to build, preserve, and transfer their wealth with the same care and intention that helped him succeed. Whether it’s financial planning, investment management, or tax strategies, he provides an evidence-based approach built on macroeconomic analysis and quantitative research to safeguard your legacy for the next generation.

Outside of work, Joshua is passionate about family. Living in the adventure sports capital, he has many hobbies, including exploring the outdoors. He also has extensive knowledge of the food and wine industry.

Full description:
Josh Bergman, JD, CFA®, is a Wealth Advisor based in Long Island, NY.

Before becoming a Wealth Advisor, Josh began his career as an attorney in the Corporate department of the law firm Simpson, Thacher & Bartlett LLP. He then transitioned into advising domestic and international UHNW individuals and families on income, gift and estate tax planning, business succession planning, and charitable giving as a Trusts & Estates attorney.

Prior to joining Savvy, Josh served as Vice President in the Wealth Management group of Allen & Company Investment Advisors, where his team of advisors managed approximately $4.5 billion of assets under management on behalf of UHNW individuals and institutional investors.

His overall career experiences make him remarkably unique. As a JD, CFA®, and someone with experience managing several billion dollars on behalf of individuals and institutions, he provides clients with broad-ranging advice that typically would require bringing in specialists from multiple disciplines.
FAQ answer 1:
Earlier in my career, I worked as a Trusts & Estates (T&E) attorney, advising ultra-high-net-worth (UHNW) individuals. In this role, I had the privilege of discussing some of the most important and sensitive topics with individuals and families, including their family dynamics, legacy, charitable intentions, and, often, their succession plans for family businesses they had worked so hard to build.

While serving as legal counsel to my clients, I discovered my passion for working with people and helping them navigate and simplify some of life’s most complex and stressful moments. This led me to an introduction to Allen & Company’s Wealth Management division, where the focus was on providing financial advice and tax guidance to UHNW families and institutional investors. Initially, Allen & Company sought to bring me in to focus exclusively on T&E planning for their clients, but I expressed an interest in offering both T&E advice and financial guidance. They supported this ambition, in part because of my background in finance and accounting, which I studied during my undergraduate years, as well as my experience working at Wharton while attending the University of Pennsylvania Law School.

At Allen & Company, I earned the Chartered Financial Analyst® designation and worked closely with families and institutions on strategic and tactical asset allocation opportunities, tax guidance, and succession planning. Over time, I served on a team that collectively advised on approximately $4.5 billion in assets under management before ultimately launching my own firm, JNB Wealth.
FAQ answer 2: I still work with UHNW families, though I am also expanding my client base to “everyday investors” who could use some help on their endeavors to retire sooner, or seek to buy a little more house, or send their children to a better school. One of the (many) reasons that I chose Savvy is that the platform provides me with the technology and operational efficiencies to work with a broader range of clients.
FAQ answer 3:
My expertise spans a few key areas that include tax and succession planning, concentrated position management, behavioral coaching, evidence-based portfolio management, sourcing alternative investments, and family communication.

Tax and Legacy Planning - I was a practicing attorney and spent most of my legal career working with families to help them achieve their business and succession planning objectives in a structure that maximized their wealth, net of income, gift, and estate taxes.

Concentrated Position Management - I have significant experience guiding clients with respect to concentrated equity positions, including analyzing risk, income tax and transfer tax considerations.  I’ve helped CEOs and board members of public companies craft 10b5-1 selling plans to systematically reduce their exposure to concentrated holdings.

Behavioral Coaching - In my decade-plus of working with clients, I have learned that the best plan is one that the client can stick with through good times and bad.

Research-Based Portfolio Management - I believe in the importance of using data to set the baseline for decision making and for projecting ranges of outcomes. This means that I lean on academic and practitioner research to inform my views and recommendations rather than the latest short-term narrative that financial media is focusing on.

Alternative Investments - Prior to joining Savvy, I evaluated private investment opportunities on behalf of clients, with a focus on expected returns net of taxes and fees, while ensuring that my clients also preserved sufficient liquidity.

Family Communication - Finally, I believe in the importance of helping families talk effectively about their wealth so that core values can be passed to the next generation. Defining and funding a good life can mean many different things to different people, and clarifying roles and expectations can be extremely valuable when it comes to maintaining family harmony.
FAQ answer 4:
The strategies are tailored to client goals, time horizon, and ability and willingness to take risks. However, there are a few foundational principles across my strategies, including a focus on tax efficiency, maintaining a long-term orientation, an emphasis on quality, constant re-underwriting of investment theses, and operating with the conviction to act opportunistically during periods of market dislocation.

Tax Efficiency: Incorporating tax planning into portfolio management includes managing “asset location.” In other words, holding high-yielding assets in tax-advantaged accounts and lower-yielding assets in taxable accounts. It also means not day-trading portfolios and therefore not generating short-term capital gains or unnecessary transaction costs where possible.

“Long-Termism”: I am a steadfast believer in the extraordinary compounding of capital that can occur after long holding periods.  In my opinion, timing the market is incredibly dangerous.  Investors need to be right twice - selling at the top and then having the courage to buy back in after a steep decline, which is often at a very scary moment in time.  It is a cliche, but for most investors, time in the market beats timing the market.

Quality: Generally, the best businesses in the world are those that:

provide a product or service that people regularly need and where there are few good substitutes

do so better, cheaper, or faster than others

do so repeatedly, and

do it without sinking a mountain of capital and fixed costs into the ground (i.e., if they are “capital-light” businesses).

These businesses tend to earn customer loyalty, utility-like usage, and pricing power that allows for sustained earnings growth and reinvestment back into the business. When I recommend external fund managers for clients, I ensure that they adhere to a similar philosophy on quality investing over long periods.

Continuous Evaluation: Having a long-term outlook does not mean “set it and forget it”. In fact, holding investments for long periods of time should be the opposite of set it and forget it. I believe that long-term holds require a constant sense of paranoia that the investment thesis is wrong: this healthy paranoia forces difficult questions and encourages more thought and circumspection throughout the life of an investment.

Strategic and Tactical Opportunism: Crises and dislocations are natural phenomena in the markets, almost purge-like episodes following periods of relative calm. Finding clarity and conviction in these moments is difficult—plenty of capital managers have been found hiding in their caves during crises—but if an investor can successfully identify and capitalize on a dislocation, they may be rewarded over long periods of time. I plan to approach each and every day—and every crisis—with a prepared mind, and I believe my clients will be well-suited to react to these opportunities with conviction as a result.
FAQ answer 5:
My favorite part about working with clients is listening and learning about each individual’s stories, challenges, and dreams. It is a privilege to sit in the seat of the “trusted advisor,” which in the most productive relationships extends far beyond investment management.

I derive great personal satisfaction in seeing my clients achieve their goals, whether it is buying a home, fully funding their retirement, paying for a dream vacation, or enabling their child to go to the school that seemed out of reach.

Ultimately, I want my clients to feel safer and feel that they can offload their financial and life stressors to me, which is a responsibility I embrace.
FAQ answer 6:
When I was deciding where to operate my business, I did due diligence on dozens of alternatives, ranging from the bulge bracket banks to independent registered investment advisors to building my own tech stack.

After countless hours of research, in-person meetings, and tech demonstrations, it became clear to me that Savvy represents the leading edge of advisor technology. This enables advisors like myself to spend more time doing what we do best - research, portfolio management, and meeting with clients, and to spend less time on repetitive administrative tasks (which are critically important to get right but which can also be incredibly inefficient and time-consuming in legacy tech systems).

In my opinion, the most important thing to me is that Savvy’s technology platform positions me to provide  a better experience for my clients.

Dan brings 25+ years of experience in financial services together with a wide depth of financial acumen and differentiated perspective given his prior experience as both an institutional trader and sales trader. This background enables him to help guide clients through the full spectrum of financial concerns. Having invested through the bull and bear markets, he understands the importance of the big picture and that times of uncertainty can often be times of opportunity. In today's environment of economic and political uncertainty, clients need a financial compass - an experienced and trusted advisor who can help them navigate toward their financial futures with greater confidence.

Dan works with a broad spectrum of clients, including professionals, private equity executives, small business owners, and other successful individuals and families. While each client has their own unique financial goals, they all have one thing in common: appreciating the value of advice from a trusted, experienced advisor who has been through decades of boom and bust cycles.

He currently lives in Rye, New York, with his wife, Christine, and their four children, Ella, Logan, Connor, and Charlie.
FAQ answer 3:
With a background in institutional trading and investing and over 25 years of experience, I am an expert in investment allocation. Beyond technical expertise, I excel in addressing the emotional aspect of financial planning. My compassionate approach, particularly evident in assisting divorcees, underscores my commitment to guiding clients through the emotional components of their financial journeys.

On the flip side, my expertise lies in the emotional aspect. I've discovered that this is a business with two complementary dimensions. I'm there to guide my clients to whatever their goals may be like retirement, but I found that the emotional component of the business is just as important. Intro description: Hi there, I’m Matthew, and I help individuals and families bring clarity and purpose to their financial lives. I offer comprehensive financial advising beyond just investments — focusing on your full financial health, with a holistic view of where you are now and where you want to go.
Quote: I aim to create a planning experience where clients feel informed, supported, and fully understood. My focus is on clarity over complexity—helping people see the full picture so they can make decisions that align with their goals and values.
Service eyebrow 1: TAKE CONTROL OF YOUR FINANCIAL FUTURE
Service description 1: Personalized wealth management helps our clients protect their assets. We use a holistic approach to financial planning that integrates tax strategy, trust & estate planning, and risk management.
Service eyebrow 2: PRESERVATION OF YOUR LEGACY
Service description 2: We specialize in making the often complex and emotionally charged process of trust and estate planning as seamless as possible ensuring the security and preservation of a client's legacy for future generations.
Service description 3: Transition into your golden years with confidence. Our goal is to see to it that you’re prepared for the unpredictable. Let us turn your retirement dreams into actionable plans.
Service eyebrow 4: STRATEGIC, DATA-DRIVEN INVESTING TO TARGET AMBITIOUS RESULTS
Service description 4: End-to-end investment management focused on tailoring portfolios to each client’s specific circumstances and preferences. Our holistic approach will take into consideration all facets of your situation along with current economic data to optimize your portfolio's risk and return.
Full description: Matthew is an Associate Wealth Advisor at Colorado Wealth Group. Matthew graduated with his BA in Finance with a certificate in Business Law from the University of Cincinnati. He brings with him experience in the financial services industry and holds his Series 65 and the CERTIFIED FINANCIAL PLANNING (CFP®) designation. He is thrilled to have joined the CWG team where he can continue learning and get to know the clients. Outside of work, Matthew moved to Colorado in late 2022 from Cincinnati, Ohio. He spends his time skiing in the winter, and in the spring/summer he enjoys hiking, camping and golfing, but once fall comes around it is all about his Cleveland Browns.
FAQ answer 1: I became a financial advisor because I’ve always been drawn to helping people make sense of their financial lives. Money influences so many decisions, but it’s often presented in ways that feel complicated or inaccessible. I wanted to be in a role where I could simplify those concepts and give people a clearer understanding of how their financial world fits together. That belief — that everyone deserves a clear, understandable roadmap for their money — is what guided me into this profession and continues to shape how I approach my work today.
FAQ answer 2: I typically work with small business owners, retirees, pre-retirees, and high-income earners who value clarity, transparency, and a practical approach to managing their wealth. Many of the people I work with are navigating important transitions, balancing multiple priorities, or managing growing financial complexity.
FAQ answer 3: My expertise includes investment management, financial planning, and building strong client relationships. I focus on bringing together a comprehensive view of a client’s financial picture — from assets and cash flow to tax considerations and long-term planning — and helping them understand how these pieces connect.
FAQ answer 4: I frequently help clients with tax-aware planning, investment alignment, and cash-flow structure. This often includes identifying ways to better organize their finances, evaluate options across different scenarios, and create a framework that helps them make informed decisions. Each strategy is tailored to the client’s individual goals, priorities, and circumstances.
FAQ answer 5: My favorite part is seeing clients gain clarity and understanding around their finances. It’s rewarding to watch someone move from a place of uncertainty to feeling more organized, informed, and confident in the decisions ahead of them.
FAQ answer 6: I appreciate the way Savvy integrates technology, investment capabilities, and a streamlined planning experience. The platform helps create simplicity for clients by bringing their financial information together in one place and supporting real-time collaboration.

Intro description: Hi there! 👋🏼 I’m Colin. I enjoy taking the time to understand each client’s individual situation and creating strategies to help them meet their goals. It’s also important to me that my clients understand how their investments work and why their portfolio is set up in a certain manner. From crafting investment strategies to tax optimization, income planning, and preparing for milestones like retirement or college funding – I’m here to help.
Quote: I love spending time educating clients, whether they want all the details or just a high-level overview. I want to ensure that clients understand why they own certain investments, why their portfolio is set up in a certain manner.

Service description 1: Transition into your golden years with confidence, regardless of age. Our goal is to see to it that you’re prepared for the unpredictable. Let us turn your retirement dreams into actionable plans with confidence and peace of mind.

Full description:
Colin is originally from Northeast Ohio but made his way to Colorado for college and to follow his passion for the great outdoors. His career in finance began at Charles Schwab over 14 years ago, where he spent the last decade as a Financial Consultant, assisting high net worth individuals and families. Holding the title of Certified Financial Planner (CFP®), Colin thrives on nurturing enduring connections and aiding clients in reaching their financial aspirations. He has moved to Savvy to offer his clients a more tailored experience alongside our tech forward team.

Residing in Denver, he unwinds from work by indulging in activities such as hiking, camping, and mountain biking. Colin enjoys spending time outdoors with his wife, Sarah, their two children, and their dog, Oliver.
FAQ answer 1:
During my college years, I worked in a customer service and management role, where I enjoyed working with people, navigating challenging situations, and problem-solving. During this time I also had a college roommate who was an economics major and they were glued to CNBC which sparked my interests in the markets. Through a family connection, I was introduced to a Schwab advisor and found similarities between my job and the advisor's role intriguing. This realization led me to pursue a career in advising. I started at Schwab in 2010 and worked my way up to an advisory position at a brand office by 2013. After more than a decade serving as an advisor, I wake up daily to look at the markets and stay involved with the trends to offer the up to date advice to my clients.

When I joined Savvy, I began a collaborative venture with my close friend, Michaela Sullivan, who is now my partner as we join forces to assist clients. While I continue to support my individual clients, I look forward to working with Michaela on future clients and supporting each other as we grow our business. I love working with the markets and Michaela is focused on financial planning and combined we want to help our clients achieve their goals.
FAQ answer 2: I work with a diverse clientele, with a focus on those approaching or in retirement, often with portfolios exceeding $1 million. I believe in not only guiding my clients on portfolio and retirement strategies but also to building connections with their children. I offer advice not only on trust/estate planning but also on education planning for the next generation. It’s important to involve children in the process to help plan for their future.
FAQ answer 3: I like to optimize my clients financial future with services like investment and income planning, retirement strategies, tax optimization, social security planning, and guidance through life transitions and liquidity events such as divorce, property or business sales, and inheritances.
FAQ answer 4: Tailored investment strategies, personalized to individual client needs such as income planning, tax optimization, gifting, and college funding.
FAQ answer 5: I enjoy being able to analyze a client’s situation and create strategies to help them meet their goals. It’s very rewarding to see good outcomes, watch a family evolve over time and show clients how powerful investing and planning can be.
FAQ answer 6: Coming from a firm that had a lot of slow processes and archaic technology, I love how efficient and tech forward things are at Savvy. It’s great that Savvy really listens to advisor feedback and implements solutions to allow us to spend more time focusing on our clients.

Ryan Garland is a CERTIFIED FINANCIAL PLANNER® with over 13 years of experience serving high-net-worth clients with complex financial needs. Ryan specializes in helping individuals and families prepare for tax-efficient retirements, business owners navigate growth and succession, and professionals manage equity compensation or concentrated stock positions. His expertise includes complex estate and wealth transfer planning, tax strategies to minimize lifetime income taxes, and designing sustainable, tax-efficient retirement income plans. Ryan’s tax-aware investment approach ensures clients keep more of what they earn when planning for the future.

What sets Ryan apart is his ability to foster meaningful conversations that uncover his clients’ true goals, values, and aspirations. He views financial planning as a noble calling and takes pride in building clear, personalized plans. For Ryan, the most rewarding part of his work is forming genuine connections with clients, often turning professional relationships into lasting friendships.

The pivot point in my career came when my best friend, Ruth, died from Colon Cancer at 32 years old.

Full description:
Eric Kirste, CFP®, CIMA®, AIF® is the founding Principal Wealth Manager at Savvy Wealth. With a deep-rooted passion for service and enriching the lives of others, Eric found his calling as a wealth management professional early on. Eric brings over 24 years of deep experience working closely with business owners, individuals and families in transition, helping them navigate difficult changes. Compassion is important to Eric, and he helps clients who are going through a divorce or grieving the loss of a spouse or family member get through the transition to financial independence and overcome new challenges with confidence. He also helps business owners and professionals nearing retirement ensure they are best prepared for their ideal retirement lifestyle.

At Savvy, he strives to help his clients align their money with their values, provide integrated solutions to serve all of their needs and empower them to make a lifetime of smart financial decisions. Importantly, Eric is committed to keeping his clients’ best interests top of mind while offering ongoing guidance, encouragement and accountability.

With a passion for helping others, Eric has volunteered for the Foundation for Financial Planning, AARP and is the Treasurer on the Board of Wings For Widows. Eric is a native of the northwest suburbs of Chicago. He is committed to giving back to his community and serves as the Treasurer for the Prospect Heights Park District Board of Commissioners and the Old Orchard Country Club. He enjoys spending time with his wife, Alisa, their two sons, Logan and Matthew, and their rescue dog, Bear.

Education:
Among his achievements, Eric has obtained several professional certifications, including the CERTIFIED FINANCIAL PLANNER™, Certified Investment Management Analyst®, and Accredited Investment Fiduciary®. He earned a Bachelor of Science in Business Finance from Miami University in Ohio and has completed the CERTIFIED FINANCIAL PLANNER™ certification education through Northwestern University, as well as the Investment Management Education Program from the University of Chicago's Booth School of Business.

FAQ answer 2:
I work with clients across the nation, addressing a wide range of significant issues faced by individuals in their 50s, 60s, and 70s. This includes providing expertise in tax planning, wealth management, financial planning, estate planning, and optimizing social security benefits. Each client's situation is unique, requiring tailored solutions that align with their specific needs and goals.

However, it's important to note that not all clients fit into this category. I also serve as a transition specialist, assisting individuals who are undergoing significant life changes, such as transitioning into retirement, starting a nonprofit, embarking on their own business ventures or navigating the loss of a loved one. Additionally, I have experience working with clients who have experienced financial windfalls later in life.

My purpose is to understand what clients value most and help them make informed decisions on how to best utilize it. It's no longer solely about retirement; some individuals may have different aspirations and a desire to explore new opportunities. I take a personalized approach, offering guidance and carefully considering various options for their next chapter.
FAQ answer 3:
Early on, it became apparent to me that there was a need beyond a sole focus on investments for a holistic approach to financial advising. While I still do investment planning I like to look at the bigger picture of a client's financial health. Over time, I have honed my expertise in tax planning, estate planning, Social Security timing, and a comprehensive assessment of individual circumstances—beyond just a client's portfolio. Tax considerations play a significant role in a portfolio, but other aspects come into play as well.

While I provide guidance on various types of insurance, such as life, long-term care, and disability, I emphasize the importance of consulting an insurance professional once we identify areas for improvement. This process involves working closely with my clients on an annual basis, reviewing their property and casualty insurance. Cash flow budgeting and income distribution represent critical aspects that are often overlooked. Transitioning from asset accumulation to de-cumulation requires careful consideration of creating a retirement paycheck. Determining the optimal amount and method to withdraw funds, considering their financial plan, cost efficiency, and tax implications, is pivotal. This process involves a comprehensive analysis and exploration of the most suitable accounts and vehicles. It is not a mere exercise of throwing numbers around—it requires a thorough understanding of each individual's unique circumstances.
FAQ answer 4:
There are numerous types of strategies to consider depending on the clients, but recently I did a financial plan for a couple in their early to mid-sixties who plan to retire within the next one to two years. This is a great example because retirement planning can happen at any point, it’s never too late or too early to plan for retirement. It was crucial to have a conversation with them before their retirement, as it gives us time to make necessary adjustments. During a comprehensive review of their situation, I discovered many areas that needed attention.

Firstly, their home insurance coverage was inadequate, especially considering the possibility of natural disasters causing significant damage. They had recently completed a major remodel, which their insurance didn't account for. Additionally, they didn't have sufficient umbrella insurance to protect them.

I also delved into their tax returns and found opportunities for optimization. Although they were generous in their charitable contributions, we helped them establish a more efficient and strategic approach to maximize the impact of their donations. Furthermore, I realized their estate plan didn't align with their desired legacy goals of leaving money to both charities and their children.

In terms of investments, the couple was overly aggressive and concerned about the level of risk they were taking. Through a thorough financial and retirement plan, I was able to provide them with a sense of security by reducing their overall risk exposure. We also made adjustments to their investment portfolio to enhance tax efficiency, incorporating direct indexing.

Lastly, I assisted them in determining the optimal time to begin taking Social Security benefits and developed a tax-efficient income distribution plan for their retirement years.

While this is just a glimpse into the services I provided, it showcases my commitment to addressing their specific needs and goals.

Michael Most has dedicated the last 27 years to the ever-evolving landscape of the financial services industry. FAQ answer 1:
In 1996, I unexpectedly found my way into the financial advising realm at American Express Financial Advisors. Over the next 17 years, I wore various hats within the organization, transitioning from an advisor to a training manager and eventually a district manager.

Initially joining the firm as American Express Financial Advisors, the name changed to Ameriprise Financial in 2005. My journey involved significant time in management, where I trained new advisors, participated in client appointments, and crafted financial plans. However, after nearly a decade in management, I felt a strong pull to return to my roots and be a financial advisor once again.
FAQ answer 2: My client base has evolved to focus on business owners and executives.
FAQ answer 3: My expertise lies in the realm of retirement planning, where I specialize in preserving, growing, and generating retirement income. This extends to individuals who are at the stage of considering stepping away from their current endeavors, even if the term "retire" might not precisely capture their future plans. These individuals have typically reached a point where they've accumulated enough financial resources to explore different career paths, even if they are not as financially lucrative.
FAQ answer 4:
When it comes to planning for retirement, my approach varies based on the individual's proximity to retirement. For those in their 20s and 30s, the emphasis is on aggressive growth since time is on their side. However, it's crucial to balance this by avoiding the pitfall of being "retirement rich" and struggling day-to-day, considering that most assets can't be accessed until after 59 and a half.

In their 40s, the strategy maintains a balance, leaning slightly towards ensuring that their retirement assets are robust and ready when needed. As clients enter their 50s or 60s, a more conservative approach is adopted. This stage involves preserving, growing, and generating income. The focus shifts from aggressive growth to maintaining a stable financial foundation while still incorporating some equity exposure to outpace inflation.

When it comes to wealth generation, many individuals use model portfolios, funds, and similar instruments. My approach involves a diversified mix, incorporating mutual funds, alternative investments such as real estate investment trusts, and blue-chip stocks. While mutual funds and alternative investments may offer stability over the long term, integrating quality stocks introduces the potential for higher returns. However, the addition of stocks requires careful selection, seeking blue-chip stocks with the worst-case scenario being a flat performance while continuing to generate dividends.
FAQ answer 5:
My favorite aspect of working with clients as a financial advisor is the genuine connection I build with them. Many of my clients have evolved into friends over time. Establishing relationships with clients allows me to gain a profound understanding of their lives, personalities, habits, and routines.

It's crucial to recognize and address the unique needs of clients, especially those who are risk-averse but still seek growth. I've developed effective communication strategies to put them at ease. The goal is to design financial plans that not only cater to their requirements but also helps to  ensure peace of mind. For clients with a higher risk tolerance, I understand that it doesn't necessitate taking excessive risks. If a modest rate of return can meet their goals, exceeding that becomes an added bonus. Striking this balance helps to ensure that clients feel secure in their financial decisions without losing sleep at night.
FAQ answer 6:
Working with Savvy has been a distinctive experience for me. Having previously been associated with larger companies, I appreciate the desire to do things differently. At Savvy, I find the space to communicate ideas freely. I value the openness to being wrong because it provides an opportunity for dialogue and learning. If someone can explain why I might be wrong, it's a chance to either course-correct or confidently defend my perspective.

Savvy's ability to swiftly turn ideas into action is impressive. They possess the capacity to not only support but also elevate your initiatives to the next level. While I've always considered myself efficient working independently, the collaborative environment at Savvy makes me hopeful that I can achieve even more by running faster and further with their team.

The biggest benefit of partnering with Savvy vs. a larger firm or working independently is that a boutique firm like Savvy can course-correct more quickly. Moreover, Savvy's cutting-edge technology and I feel their adaptability to the evolving landscape set them apart. In a world where technology, especially AI, is rapidly advancing, I want to embrace and leverage these changes to benefit those I work with.

As for prospective clients, I believe in one-on-one relationships. People will either like you or they won't, and it's important to avoid letting ego dictate. I'm here to earn your business and would love the opportunity to talk and see if we align.

Full description:
Bruce Larsen has been helping individuals and families pursue financial security for more than 30 years. His career began in accounting after earning a Bachelor of Science in Accounting from the University of Wyoming in 1988. After nine years in accounting, Bruce transitioned to personal financial planning, where he developed a particular expertise in retirement income, tax planning, estate planning, and Social Security.

In 2020, Bruce brought his practice to Colorado Wealth Group, where he continues to work with clients while collaborating with other advisors and professionals to provide comprehensive financial planning. His approach is highly integrated, recognizing that investment decisions, retirement income, taxes, Social Security, insurance, and estate planning are interconnected.
Bruce has a particular passion for helping clients make informed decisions about taxes in retirement. He is an Enrolled Agent (EA), giving him a strong foundation in federal taxation, and has written a book focused on taxes in retirement. He also developed Tax Acuity, a tax-planning application designed to help financial advisors identify and implement tax-planning opportunities for their clients.

For more than 25 years, Bruce has also specialized in special-needs planning, helping families address the unique financial, estate-planning, and long-term care challenges associated with disability and special-needs situations. He is a Certified Estate Planner™ (CEP®), a designation focused on estate-planning essentials including living trusts, estate taxes, disability and special-needs planning, and related topics.

Bruce's philosophy is centered on helping clients understand not just where they are financially, but how today's decisions can affect their financial security years or even generations into the future. His practice takes a multi-generational approach, working with clients and, when appropriate, helping coordinate planning across their family tree.

Bruce grew up on a cattle ranch in Wyoming and has called Colorado home since 2008. He has a grown son and daughter and enjoys spending time with family, life on his Colorado ranch, team roping, and spending time outdoors.

Hi 👋🏼 I'm Albert. I advise corporate executives, entrepreneurs, and wealth-builders to shift from the noise of managing financial complexity to a state of total clarity, backed by a custom blueprint deliberately aligned with what matters most in life.

At our practice, we believe building wealth is just the baseline. Many professionals and business owners reach a threshold where they’ve achieved incredible career milestones, yet find a more profound question emerging: How do I align these resources to live with deep intentionality? We step in as dedicated partners at that exact crossroad, guiding our clients as they streamline their financial moving pieces so they can focus on the experiences, people, and pursuits that give life true meaning.

Together, we transform wealth from a complex web of numbers into a protective, highly optimized engine to give you the ultimate freedom to accomplish what really matters today and secure your legacy for tomorrow.

Full description:
My trajectory in wealth management bridges rigorous institutional experience with an independent, entrepreneurial drive. Spanning more than two decades in global financial markets, I have dedicated my career to decoding complex economic landscapes for professionals, multi-generational families, and business owners.

I am a graduate of the Lubar College of Business at the University of Wisconsin-Milwaukee, and I hold the Certified Private Wealth Advisor® (CPWA®) designation, an advanced credential completed through the Yale University School of Management. The CPWA® curriculum requires a multidisciplinary mastery of advanced wealth management disciplines, specifically focusing on complex tax mitigation, asset protection, estate preservation, and legacy structures. This specialized training allows me to look at wealth through a wide-angle lens, protecting clients against concentrated market risks, minimizing structural tax drag, and smoothing the transition of family assets. Prior to aligning with Savvy, I successfully founded and scaled my own independent advisory firm, Marketwise Asset Management, establishing a deep-seated commitment to providing institutional-grade portfolio oversight delivered through a warm, deeply individualized client experience fluent in both domestic and international dynamics.
FAQ answer 1:
Long before navigating private wealth, there were green-screen spreadsheets.

Growing up, the financial world wasn't just an abstract concept; it was a frequent backdrop to daily life. My mother dedicated her career to JPMorgan Chase, and walking through those bustling corporate corridors as a kid sparked an early fascination with how global wealth moves. By high school, while my peers were exploring other interests, I was completely absorbed in personal finance courses and early spreadsheet design. I later paired this analytical mindset with practical technical experience, working within my university's IT infrastructure department while earning my degree in finance and marketing.

My professional career took root at The Bank of New York Clearing (now Pershing LLC), but an unexpected chapter soon took me back to my birth country of Venezuela. There, I immersed myself in international wealth management, handling private client portfolios for major institutions like CitiGold Private Client and StateTrust. Working alongside elite, seasoned executives taught me how to manage deep financial complexity, but it also crystallized my desire to build an independent practice focused entirely on client alignment.

Following rigorous study and insightful strategic mentorship at the New York Institute of Finance, I took the entrepreneurial leap and established Marketwise Asset Management in Florida in 2012. Operating an independent firm for a decade grounded me in the realities of business ownership—understanding the unique exposures business owners face, the real-world weight of critical financial choices, and the absolute necessity of transparent advice. I brought that exact blend of institutional knowledge and independent care to Savvy.
FAQ answer 2:
We primarily serve corporate executives, senior managers, and business owners who have achieved substantial professional success and require a higher level of financial coordination to protect what they’ve built.

Many of our clients are what we consider intentional builders. They look beyond basic stock picking; they are navigating pivotal, complex transitions—whether that involves unwinding a highly concentrated equity position, structuring a business for an eventual exit, navigating cross-border assets, or establishing an estate framework for the next generation. They value an advisor who fluently speaks both the language of corporate strategy and family dynamics, and who can help them optimize their assets to focus on what truly matters in life.
FAQ answer 3: In the ever-evolving markets of today, I am dedicated to providing meticulous and forward-thinking investment management solutions. My career focus lies in investment management, equity analysis, and financial planning, aimed at aiding clients in tax planning, executive compensation and portfolio management. Each client strategy is rigorously tailored, considering factors such as tax implications, liquidity, and risk tolerance. I devote personal attention to every portfolio, recognizing that each client possesses unique investment goals, aiming to align opportunities with objectives.
FAQ answer 4: We help clients construct financial blueprints that mirror the life they want to lead. Every client relationship starts with a clean slate and a goals-based planning process, never a standardized model. From there, we deploy specific, advanced mechanisms tailored to your exact career and lifestyle stage. For corporate executives facing concentrated equity risks or restricted stock issues, we implement protective strategies such as equity collars, covered call writing, or exchange funds to systematically diversify positions while managing capital gains exposure. For our business owners, we emphasize early pre-sale planning and trust mapping to insulate business value long before a transaction occurs. For those approaching retirement, we systematically restructure wealth into predictable, tax-efficient income systems designed to replace a corporate salary seamlessly.
FAQ answer 5:
For me, it is the opportunity to step past the balance sheets and build a deep, human connection that goes far beyond a traditional, transactional business relationship. I want to be the steady, reliable support my clients can lean on when life brings unexpected changes, major transitions, or complex decisions.

There is immense satisfaction in helping someone strip away the financial noise and navigate the intricacies of wealth so they can focus entirely on what brings them joy. When a client realizes their assets are organized, fully optimized, and actively serving their true purpose in life, you can physically see the weight lift off their shoulders. Becoming that trusted, lifelong anchor for a family to help them protect what matters most. This is exactly why I do this work.
FAQ answer 6: I love how dynamic the team is within operations and advisor support. The technology platform is outstanding for both clients and advisors. But most importantly, I encounter amazing human beings throughout the organization!
